messages:
Alex: Hey — debugging a 502 a customer saw in prod. They sent request_id=req_7b9f3c and span id=span-4a12. Console trace shows only a partial path. What's the fastest way to pull raw logs end-to-end (edge -> ingress -> pod) to stitch this together?

Priya: @Alex — quickest path is traces in Console -> click the span -> 'Open related logs'. If that link is missing, fall back to stern on the pod. Typical pattern: 
```
# find pod from trace metadata or label
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=my-service
# tail logs and grep for the request id
stern -n prod my-service --since 30m | rg "req_7b9f3c"
```

Sam: Also check envoy/edge logs. They usually have the x-request-id header. Example: 
```
stern -n edge envoy --since 1h | rg req_7b9f3c
```
That often gives you the ingress timestamp to correlate with pod logs.

Alex: I tried Console but the span didn't include service.name tag — only trace id. Any quick trace->request_id mapping?

Priya: We have an internal lookup service for that: 
```
curl -s "https://reqlinker.internal.prod/lookup?trace=span-4a12" | jq .
```
It returns the best-known request_id and the pod that handled it (if available).

Sam: If reqlinker is unreachable, fallback options: check for Kubernetes labels (we started adding trace_id label on recent releases):
```
kubectl -n prod get pods --selector=trace_id=span-4a12 -o wide
# or brute-force logs if labels aren't present
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=my-service --tail=200 | rg "span-4a12|req_7b9f3c"
```
If you find the pod, stern is still the fastest for multi-container rotation.

DevOps-bot: FYI — if the root span was sampled out you might only see partial traces. You can temporarily bump trace sampling/retention in the observability console (ping @oncall for permission). :information_source:

Alex: Nice — reqlinker returned the pod name, I ran stern and found the full request payload and a 502 from upstream with an upstream timeout. Found the upstream latency spikes around the same timestamp. Thanks! :tada:

Priya: Great. Follow-up: I'll add an alert annotation that includes the x-req-id when 5xx spike triggers so hunts are faster. Assigning to @Sam to tune thresholds and add a dashboard quick-link to reqlinker.

Sam: Sounds good — I'll add a small panel for request_id distribution and a link to reqlinker in the service dashboard. ETA EOD.
